title: The purifier that stopped reporting contamination
brief: A water-processing team wants to deploy a new controller because its randomized trial recorded fewer contamination failures. Decide what the supplied evidence establishes about actual contamination, what remains undecided, and what a practical next investigation must change. Give a self-contained technical recommendation in ordinary prose, using calculations when useful. Resolve the disagreement between the two reviewers; neither is an authority. Show at least two materially different underlying explanations compatible with the records, and explain what would discriminate them. Treat these as synthetic stipulated facts; external research is unnecessary. Do not substitute a general caution about correlation for analysis of this particular randomized experiment. You may preserve an initial conclusion if the objections do not defeat its actual reasons.

sources.name: trial_protocol_and_endpoint
sources.text: Merewater runs isolated processing cycles. Each cycle receives controller OFF or ON by an independent fair random assignment made before the cycle. There is no interference, carryover, assignment failure, or treatment-dependent loss of a cycle from the operations ledger. ON bundles a mechanical wall scraper with optical signal smoothing. OFF uses neither. No other operating setting differs. The scraper might remove attached material or release it into the outgoing water; its net effect is not stipulated. Define Y=1 to mean that outgoing water at minute 12 exceeds the stipulated viable-organism threshold. The scientific question is the effect of assigning ON rather than OFF on the probability of Y=1 across all cycles, not the frequency of alarms or failure records. For this thought experiment, the supplied arm proportions are exact experimental probability masses expressed as counts out of 200 equally weighted cycles per arm. Ignore sampling error: this isolates identification from statistical precision. Random assignment identifies an arm's complete outcome distribution if that distribution can actually be observed.

sources.name: operations_records
sources.text: Each arm has 200 cycles. OFF: 160 cycles had optical sampling eligibility S=1; all 160 were independently assayed, with 32 Y=1 and 128 Y=0. The remaining 40 cycles had S=0 and no assay. ON: 80 cycles had S=1; all 80 were independently assayed, with 8 Y=1 and 72 Y=0. The remaining 120 cycles had S=0 and no assay. Every unassayed Y value is genuinely unavailable. No assay record was lost after a sample had been collected. A failure record requires both S=1 and Y=1. The eligibility signal S is obtained before collecting the minute-12 sample. S has no physical effect on processing, and operators took no downstream action during the trial in response to S. These are the complete outcome observations. There is no validated deterministic relation or calibrated sensitivity bound between S and Y.

sources.name: sampling_implementation_addendum
sources.text: The protocol summary contains the exact sentence: 'Sampling slots were chosen randomly before controller assignment.' This is true: a pretrial random schedule chose the minute-12 slot from several possible inspection slots for each cycle. It did not choose an unconditional assay sample of cycles. The implemented collection robot opened its sample valve at that slot only if the optical gate reported S=1. If S=0, it collected nothing and retained no material for later assay. Thus every scheduled slot existed, but collection was conditional on a post-assignment signal. An engineering calibration with a fixed optical input showed that smoothing can change S without changing the fluid. That establishes a possible measurement path from ON to eligibility. It does not establish how much of the observed arm difference follows that path, and it does not establish the scraper's effect on Y.

sources.name: independent_assay_validation
sources.text: The collected sample was sealed immediately and labeled with a random identifier. An independent laboratory used the stipulated viable-culture assay, not the plant's optical fluorescence estimate. For this synthetic task, the assay reports the sampled cycle's Y exactly. Sample collection and assay do not change the preceding minute-12 fluid state. Controller setting, smoothing, scraper use, and sample labels cannot distort the assay readout once a sample exists. This validation says nothing about uncollected cycles. The plant's dashboard misleadingly calls both an optical indication and a laboratory result a 'contamination check'; the raw operations table above disambiguates them.

sources.name: deployment_pitch_and_reviews
sources.text: The deployment pitch says: 'Recorded contamination failures fell by 75 percent under randomized assignment, so actual contamination fell by 75 percent.' It cites the sampling-slots sentence as proof that the assay observations are an unbiased sample of all cycles. Reviewer Mira objects that smoothing may hide contaminated cycles, but then goes further: 'The optical controller corrupts the laboratory test itself, so even the 32 and 8 positive results tell us nothing about actual organisms. Throw the entire trial away.' Reviewer Noel replies: 'Mira's laboratory-corruption claim is false. Also, within assayed cycles the failure rate is 20 percent with OFF and 10 percent with ON. Because assignment was random and slots were random, ON therefore halves actual contamination. We can approve deployment.' Both reviewers have read the same files. No other measurements exist.

sources.name: followup_options_and_scope
sources.text: The team can rerun randomized ON/OFF cycles. It can program unconditional sample collection at minute 12, or select cycles for collection with a known random probability independently of controller assignment, S, and the fluid. The laboratory can assay either kind of collected sample. It can also retain S even when the valve is opened unconditionally. Engineering can independently toggle the scraper and signal smoothing for a later factorial study. The immediate question is whether ON reduces the actual minute-12 contamination probability; longer-term health effects, costs, and any safety threshold for approval are outside these stipulated facts. Merely collecting more cycles with the old optical-gated collection rule is also possible. Explain whether that addresses the difficulty.

assessment.intended_difficulty: Separate random treatment assignment from post-treatment ascertainment; retain a misleading quotation as literally true while rejecting its deployment use; reject a mistaken assay criticism without treating that rejection as vindication of the pitch; expose nonidentification constructively and propose a feasible discriminating intervention. The difficult point is that two genuine improvements in the observed records can coexist with either sign of the actual contamination effect.
expected_reasoning: The recorded-failure probability is 32/200=0.16 OFF and 8/200=0.04 ON, an absolute reduction of 0.12, or 12 percentage points, and 75 percent relative to OFF. These are effects on the recorded composite event S=1,Y=1, not identified effects on Y itself.

The assayed conditional failure rates are 32/160=0.20 and 8/80=0.10. Conditioning on post-treatment S selects different subsets. Treatment randomization and preassignment slot randomization do not imply random inclusion in those assayed subsets. No assumption licenses Y independence from S within an arm, missing-at-random imputation, or treating S=0 as Y=0.

With no information about unassayed outcomes, OFF's actual failure probability lies in [32/200,72/200]=[0.16,0.36]; ON's lies in [8/200,128/200]=[0.04,0.64]. The ON-minus-OFF risk contrast lies in [-0.32,+0.48]. The stated exact-probability idealization makes these identification bounds rather than confidence intervals. Reporting the bounds is useful but an equally sound constructive argument can establish the core uncertainty without them.

One compatible beneficial world has no positives among either arm's unassayed cycles: actual contamination is 16 percent OFF and 4 percent ON. One compatible harmful world has no positives among the 40 unassayed OFF cycles and 100 positives among the 120 unassayed ON cycles: actual contamination is 16 percent OFF and 54 percent ON. Both preserve every supplied observed count and the real quote; random assignment does not rule out either arm-specific potential-outcome distribution. A no-effect world is also possible, for example 0 unassayed positives OFF and 24 ON, yielding 16 percent in both arms. Alternative consistent constructions and broader bounds are acceptable if correctly scoped.

A compatible physical account is that scraping reduces actual contamination while smoothing lowers sampling eligibility; another is that scraping releases viable organisms while smoothing disproportionately removes contaminated cycles from assay eligibility. The bench calibration establishes that smoothing can affect eligibility, not that it explains the whole record or that all physical effects vanish. These are candidate accounts, not established mechanisms.

Mira's claim that ON corrupts the independent viable-culture assay contradicts the stipulated assay validation. Her narrower ascertainment concern remains valid. The observed positives and negatives are real for the sampled cycles. Rejecting the assay-corruption objection does not restore Noel's unsupported inference about all cycles; preserving a no-safety-benefit-established conclusion on the remaining reason is legitimate correction.

Rerandomize ON/OFF and collect all minute-12 samples regardless of S, or use known random inclusion independent of assignment, S, and fluid. The assay then observes a representative outcome distribution for the causal comparison; retain S to study ascertainment. A factorial scraper-by-smoothing design with unconditional assays can distinguish component effects and measurement effects. Random audit of otherwise unassayed cycles with correct stratum weighting is also sound. More cycles under unchanged gated sampling only sharpen the observed composite and conditional quantities, not recover missing outcomes without added assumptions.

The trial supports a reduction in recorded failures under the stated randomization, while the sign of actual contamination change is unresolved. It does not by itself justify deployment on a claim of reduced actual contamination. An appropriate recommendation can be provisional and decisive about the need for different ascertainment without claiming the device is harmful, safe, useless, or globally unidentifiable in principle.
decisive_constraints: All sources are visible to both experimental conditions; assessment material is withheld. No answer may require an unmentioned biological mechanism, outside paper, hidden threshold, or additional measurement.
The true quotation cannot establish random unconditional sample inclusion because the addendum explicitly supplies the collection gate.
Independent assays are exact for collected samples; missingness is the defect. Invalidating the assay or dismissing all existing observations violates the stipulated facts.

Both signs of the Y effect and zero effect are compatible with the complete records. Any numerical bound must use all-cycle denominators for actual risk and must not present conditional rates as the total effect.
The followup must change ascertainment or supply a justified identifying assumption; repetition under the existing protocol alone is not enough.

Sound alternative accounts, valid paraphrases, corrected criticisms, and a useful unchanged conclusion are acceptable. No response is rewarded merely for changing its conclusion, criticizing more items, producing code, or matching exact wording.
plausible_failures: Converts the real 75 percent reduction in recorded failures into a 75 percent reduction in actual contamination.
Uses the 20-versus-10-percent conditional comparison or the true random-slots quote to claim that selection bias has been eliminated.
Repairs Mira's false criticism and then treats the remaining deployment claim as vindicated by default.
Treats no assay as a negative assay, or invents assay corruption despite the validation.
States only generic correlation cautions despite treatment being randomized, without locating post-treatment ascertainment.
Claims the controller definitely harms, does nothing, or acts entirely through smoothing because one compatible account has been found.
Proposes only more data with the unchanged gate, or proposes a gold-standard assay without ensuring representative sample collection.
Produces elaborate process discussion while omitting an actionable answer about what is known and what observation would distinguish the competing accounts.
assessment.negative_case: A harness output that drops the assay-validation qualification, accepts the random-slots quote as semantic support, adds unsupported mechanistic certainty, or loses a correct nonidentification argument already present in its first contribution counts against usefulness on this task. If direct and harness answers preserve the same sound analysis while the harness spends more tokens or latency, that is no observed explanatory benefit for this configuration; it is not a proof about every harness or creativity. A response may remain unchanged after correcting Mira if the missingness reason survives.
